subject.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes

question: Should semantically uncertain Skill Workshop updates override the `auto` approval policy and require pre-write human review, or must automatic apply remain unconditional for every syntactically valid proposal?
rationale: Syntax validation cannot reliably distinguish a complete skill rewrite from a plan document, so closing the remaining data-loss path requires choosing how the recently intentional automatic-approval policy behaves under uncertainty.

options.title: Review uncertain updates
options.body: Keep automatic apply for objectively valid, high-confidence proposals but force pending approval with a bounded diff when update content cannot be safely classified.

options.title: Keep unconditional automatic apply
options.body: Limit apply validation to objective syntax and integrity checks, preserving automatic apply while accepting generation quality as the primary semantic safeguard.

recommendation.title: Review uncertain updates
recommendation.body: Keep automatic apply for objectively valid, high-confidence proposals but force pending approval with a bounded diff when update content cannot be safely classified.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged change introduced the automatic-approval behavior whose safety semantics require clarification.
